image_description: A white minibus with a dark lower trim, parked on a muddy surface. The vehicle features a high roof, a large front windshield, side windows along the passenger cabin, and standard van wheels. There are visible reflections in the windows and some dirt/mud splatter on the lower body panels.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Boxy body shape noticeably shorter than a full-size bus, yet tall enough for passengers to stand or sit upright comfortably.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vehicle clearly exhibits the characteristic high-roof, boxy silhouette of a minibus (likely a Ford Transit or similar chassis). It is visibly shorter than a full-size city bus but tall enough for standing headroom.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Large windshield and row of side windows along passenger area.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A large, single-pane windshield is present. A continuous row of rectangular side windows runs along the passenger compartment, consistent with minibus design.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Height is substantial, with entrance door at front or mid-body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vehicle has significant height relative to its width. The driver's door is visible at the front, and the sliding passenger door track/handle area is implied at the mid-body position typical for this class.
While the door is closed, the panel gaps and handle placement on the side correspond to a sliding door mechanism common in minibuses. No hinge artifacts suggesting a swing door are visible.
The short hood/nose section ahead of the windshield indicates a front-engine layout, typical for van-based minibuses.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rear flat or slightly angled panel with taillights and license plate mount.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rear of the vehicle is not visible in the frame; it is cut off by the image boundary.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: White, yellow, or company livery paint with route markings.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vehicle is painted white with a dark grey/black lower cladding. There appears to be faint text or graphics on the side panel, though indistinct.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Standard van-sized wheels with steel or alloy rims.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The wheels are proportional to the vehicle size, appearing to be standard steel rims with hubcaps, consistent with commercial vans/minibuses.
The window count and body length suggest a capacity within the 4-10 passenger range, fitting the definition of a minibus rather than a full-size coach.

artifact_observations.location: Lower side panel and wheel wells
artifact_observations.reasoning: The mud/dirt texture on the lower body looks slightly smudged and lacks fine particulate detail, blending into the paint in a way that suggests minor generative smoothing or low-resolution texture mapping.
The vertical pillars between the side windows show very slight irregularities in thickness and alignment, though this could also be attributed to the angle of view and reflection.

The background elements (trees/structures) are heavily blurred, which is consistent with depth-of-field but also common in AI generations to mask lack of detail. The transition between the sharp vehicle and blurred background is relatively clean but worth noting.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific make/model classification and ensure it aligns with the 'minibus' label rather than a full-size bus or cargo van.
To verify the structural integrity of the wheels contacting the ground and the planar consistency of the side panels.
To check for melting or fusion artifacts around complex boundaries like window seals and door handles.
To assess the realism of the mud textures and lighting reflections on the glossy paint.

focus_areas: Wheel-ground contact points for physical plausibility
Texture consistency of mud splatter vs. painted surface
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the wheel geometry; AI often struggles with elliptical perspective on rims. Check if the mud texture looks like applied noise rather than accumulated dirt. Verify that the side windows maintain consistent spacing and perspective convergence towards the rear.
